newsitem.title: UK: Burundi refugees face new peril, Amnesty says.
newsitem.headline: Burundi refugees face new peril, Amnesty says.

text.p: Refugees forced by Tutsi-led armed groups in eastern Zaire to return home to Burundi are in danger of further atrocities, the human rights group Amnesty International said on Thursday.
"These refugees are being forced back to Burundi to face the same terrible human rights abuses that caused them to flee in the first place," the London-based group said in a statement.
"No refugees should be forcibly returned to a country which has seen as many as 500 returnees reportedly killed by the Burundi security forces in recent weeks."

The human rights organisation said it had documented cases of killings, disappearances and ill-treatment occurring almost daily throughout Burundi, with women, children, babies and the elderly among the victims.
Burundian Hutu refugees fled Burundi two years ago to escape violence and death following the massacre of up to one million Tutsis in neighbouring Rwanda.
Burundian Prime Minister Pascal Firmin Ndimira said on Tuesday that more than 30,000 out of an estimated 150,000 refugees had returned from eastern Zaire.
Amnesty is calling on governments to condemn the Tutsi-led armed groups in eastern Zaire for forcing the refugees to return home, and the Zairean authorities for stating that they may not remain.

"It is completely unacceptable for governments to remain silent and refuse to condemn this appalling situation. While these governments concentrate on events in Rwanda and their desire to resolve the current refugee problem, the fate of those refugees who have fled Burundi should not be ignored."
